items.summary: Nitrogen-doped Tungsten-Rhenium superconducting alloys were recently proposed as a promising material platform for superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs), offering a favorable balance between high normal state resistivity and tunable superconducting properties. In this work, we report on the fabrication and characterization of SNSPDs based on thin W0.75Re0.25 films deposited by reactive DC magnetron sputtering in a mixed Ar/N2 atmosphere. Meander detectors with 70 nm linewidth exhibit saturated internal detection efficiency (IDE) up to 1310 nm and 85.3% IDE at 1550 nm at 2.5 K, with sub-nanosecond rise times, decay times of the order of a few nanoseconds, and timing jitter of 73.2 ps measured with room temperature amplifiers.

items.title: Critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation
items.summary: We investigate the critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation, which remain connected after the removal of any two sites. By combining biconnected-component decomposition with the SPQR decomposition of graphs, we develop an efficient algorithm for identifying triconnected clusters in large systems. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations yield estimates of the fractal dimension $d_3=1.2308(3)$, $1.083(2)$, and $0.77(2)$ in dimensions $d=2$, $3$, and $4$, respectively, revealing a systematic decrease of $d_3$ with increasing $d$. In dimension $d=6$, the largest triconnected cluster grows logarithmically with system size, whereas on complete graphs, corresponding to $d=\infty$, it approaches a finite size. Both behaviors indicate a vanishing fractal dimension, $d_3=0$, for $d\geq6$. Furthermore, the singular contribution to the susceptibility-like quantity associated with the second moment of the triconnected-cluster size distribution scales as $χ\sim L^{2d_3-d}$. Consequently, it vanishes for $d\geq3$, leaving a finite asymptotic susceptibility, in contrast to the divergent behavior observed in standard percolation.

items.title: Effective field theories of nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics in one dimension
items.summary: Describing emergent macroscopic phenomena in low spatial dimensions is known to be notoriously challenging, primarily due to strong interactions that render perturbative approaches inapplicable. On the other hand, low-dimensional systems host a wealth of unorthodox phenomena. A prominent example is the emergence of superdiffusive transport in one-dimensional interacting systems, traditionally studied in the framework of nonlinear fluctuating hydrodynamics. After identifying and discussing internal inconsistencies in the previous formulations, in this work we develop a general and systematic approach for constructing effective field theories of one-dimensional hydrodynamic systems in the form of coupled stochastic Langevin-type equations compatible with the physical requirements of local equilibrium states - the thermodynamic Maxwell relation and fluctuation-dissipation symmetry. To exemplify our construction, we devise a numerical integration scheme and implement it on a simple model of two interacting hydrodynamic modes with a non-Gaussian stationary equilibrium measure.

items.title: Plasmon excitations in monolayer stanene
items.summary: Monolayer stanene exhibits strong intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and notably distinct low-energy band features involving both $Γ$ and K valleys together with strong electron-hole asymmetry among group-IV monolayers. Its plasmonic properties and external-field tunability remain largely unclarified. Here, we systematically investigate its high-energy plasmon structures and low-energy collective excitation modulated by temperature, electrostatic doping and perpendicular electric field. Calculations use a $sp^3$ tight-binding model with SOC and sublattice staggered potentials, combined with the finite-temperature multiband Lindhard function under the random-phase approximation. Besides the $π$ and $π+σ$ plasmon known in graphene/silicene, stanene supports two new high-energy plasmon branches. For low-energy plasmons, thermal excitation extends the accessible energy-momentum range while preserving high quality factors and collective coherence. Electrostatic doping yields distinct plasmon behaviors: moderate doping gives K-valley dominated intraband $\sqrt{q}$ Dirac plasmons; heavy electron doping retains $\sqrt{q}$ dispersion via Drude contributions from $Γ$ and K valleys; heavy hole doping triggers interband transitions near the $Γ$ point, producing new $σ$-$σ$ and $σ$-$σ^*$ interband plasmon modes and complex multi-branch spectra. Furthermore, the perpendicular electric field enables continuous tuning of the $\sqrt{q}$ plasmon via band reconstruction below 0.3 V/Å and induces extra plasmon modes near band-gap closure. These tunable low-energy plasmons span terahertz-to-mid-infrared frequencies, promising for nanophotonic applications.

items.title: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
items.summary: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure. While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe3 achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.

items.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
items.summary: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl- induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between -40 and 85 degrees C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

items.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
items.summary: Intrinsic color centers are investigated in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation delta SCF calculations identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. A comparison of their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It exhibits the highest calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate of 43.9 MHz and ZPL quantum efficiency of 11.8% among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation yields a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a multimode photoluminescence calculation gives a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37%, indicating a dominant zero-phonon contribution. The predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) also has the smallest photon-energy separation from the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets among the candidates. These results identify VVa1+ as a promising intrinsic color center for fiber-based quantum communication, with quantum frequency upconversion offering a route from its strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands.

items.title: Lyapunov spectrum scaling transition for quasiperiodic nonlinear unitaries
items.summary: We study the Lyapunov spectrum scaling of thermal weakly-nonlinear unitary maps in the presence of quasiperiodic potentials. We search for the crossover from long-range to short-range scaling as the localization length ξ decreases and compare the details to the case of uncorrelated Anderson disorder [Phys. Rev. Res. 6 L012064 (2024)]. A comparative statistical analysis of the eigenstates for the linear case shows that quasiperiodicity has a stronger localization impact at the same value of ξ. Therefore we expect that the scaling crossover should be enhanced as well. However, the numerical analysis shows that it is strongly delayed as compared to Anderson disorder, and is observed at anomalously small values of ξ. These findings hint at the potential impact of long range correlations of quasiperiodic localized eigenstates, which persist in the presence of interactions even in the case of integrability breaking and thermalization.

items.title: Plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekulé distortion: Electron-hole asymmetry of the effective interlayer tunneling
items.summary: The effective interlayer tunneling (EIT) is a key quantity in determining the out-of-phase plasmons of a bilayer structure. Using the tight-binding model and the random phase approximation, we investigate plasmons in bilayer graphene with O-type Kekulé distortion. Both O/O and G/O bilayers exhibit strong electron-hole asymmetry in the EIT. For the O/O bilayer, the gap of the out-of-phase plasmon remains almost constant as the electron concentration varies, whereas it increases rapidly with increasing hole concentration; hole doping can also lead to stronger anomalous dispersion than electron doping. For the G/O bilayer, enhancing the Kekulé distortion $Δ_0$ can weaken the EIT, as reflected by the reduced interlayer hybridization caused by the lifted layer degeneracy, especially for the electron-doped case. For the electron-doped G/O bilayer, the EIT is almost turned off when $Δ_0=0.3$ from the perspective of the dispersion. Our results imply that switching the doping type between electron and hole can tune the performance of out-of-phase plasmon-based devices by modulating the EIT.

items.title: On the growth of operator entanglement in brickwork circuits with Yang--Baxter gates
items.summary: We study the operator entanglement of local operators in one-dimensional brickwork circuits whose two-site gate satisfies the braid relation; throughout this work, we call such a gate a Yang--Baxter gate. We establish upper bounds for several structured, overlapping classes of Yang--Baxter gates. We show that the operator Schmidt rank remains uniformly bounded in time for all qubit Yang--Baxter gates and, in arbitrary local dimension, for permutation gates obtained from non-degenerate Yang--Baxter maps. We also show that it grows at most polynomially for involutive dual-unitary Yang--Baxter gates and for arbitrary phase dressings of permutation gates obtained from non-degenerate Yang--Baxter maps. These results imply, respectively, constant and logarithmic upper bounds on the operator entanglement. Conversely, we construct a seven-state involutive Yang--Baxter gate without dual unitarity and a one-site operator whose exact operator Schmidt rank grows exponentially, although the corresponding operator entropies remain undetermined. Entanglement growth in the general Yang--Baxter case remains open. All proofs and selected examples were constructed by ChatGPT.

items.title: Interface-Controlled Spin-Orbit Torques in Rare-Earth Synthetic Ferrimagnets Probed by Sagnac Magneto-Optics and Harmonic Hall Measurements
items.summary: Spin-orbit torque (SOT) provides an efficient route for manipulating magnetization in spintronic devices, and its accurate quantification is essential. Here, we investigate Co/Gd-based synthetic ferrimagnets using complementary magnetotransport and magneto-optical techniques. We use a Sagnac magneto-optical interferometry method to directly quantify current-induced magnetization tilting and extract the damping-like SOT effective field. The Sagnac measurements show good agreement with harmonic Hall analysis across different Co/Gd and Gd/Pt/Co heterostructures, providing a quantitative determination of the damping-like SOT effective field that does not rely on electrical transport signatures. By varying the Gd thickness and multilayer stacking order, we demonstrate that the damping-like torque is strongly influenced by spin transport and angular momentum conversion at rare-earth and heavy-metal interfaces. The observation of a finite torque in Gd/Pt/Co/Pt structures, where conventional Pt spin Hall contributions are expected to compensate, highlights the active role of the Gd layer in SOT generation. Furthermore, interface engineering enables perpendicular magnetic anisotropy in Gd/Pt/Co/Al heterostructures with a 2-nm-thick Co layer, allowing current-induced SOT switching at current densities of 8-10 MA/cm$^2$. These results establish rare-earth-based synthetic ferrimagnets as a versatile platform for engineering spin-orbit phenomena and optimizing low-power spintronic devices.

items.title: Emergent Quantized Zak Phases without Dimerization in a Multicomponent Fermionic Extended Hubbard Model
items.summary: Quantized Zak phases are commonly associated with dimerized systems, such as the noninteracting Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) model. In interacting systems, however, interactions can induce effective dimerization of particle clusters even in the absence of explicit dimerization in the underlying lattice. In this work, we study a one-dimensional multicomponent fermionic extended Hubbard model under a resonance condition between the on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions. We find that quantized Zak phases emerge for odd fermion numbers $n\geqslant 3$, protected by the inversion symmetry of the effective Hamiltonian. Furthermore, in the presence of a tilted field, fermion clusters exhibit Bloch oscillations, during which their Zak phases can be extracted from the evolution of a Gaussian wave packet over one Bloch period. Our results reveal an interaction-induced mechanism for realizing quantized Zak phases in multicomponent fermionic systems without explicit lattice dimerization.

items.title: Real-Space Visualization of Site-Selective Co 3d States in the Ising Magnet Ca3Co2O6
items.summary: High-spin Co3+ ions can retain a finite orbital contribution and exhibit pronounced magnetic anisotropy, providing model systems for Ising magnetism. However, direct real-space observations of their orbital states remain limited. Here, we visualize the site-dependent Co 3d electronic states in the Ising-chain magnet Ca3Co2O6, which contains crystallographically inequivalent high-spin and low-spin Co3+ sites, using synchrotron X-ray diffraction and valence electron density (VED) analysis based on core differential Fourier synthesis. The octahedral Co site exhibits a VED distribution consistent with a low-spin state, whereas the trigonal-prismatic Co site shows pronounced anisotropy that cannot be reproduced by crystal electric field (CEF) effects alone. A wavefunction analysis incorporating CEF effects, spin-orbit coupling, and ligand-mediated Co 3d-O 2p-Co 4p hybridization reproduces the observed VED anisotropy. These results establish a site-selective real-space picture of the Co electronic states and demonstrate the capability of VED analysis to probe local orbital states and orbital hybridization in quantum materials.

items.title: Non-Gaussian limit distributions of giant-component sizes in inhomogeneous networks
items.summary: We demonstrate that the size distribution of giant components in percolation and epidemic spreading models on highly inhomogeneous networks often fails to converge to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit. Instead, when appropriately scaled, the distribution converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD). This scaling behavior aligns with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT), which governs sums of random variables following heavy-tailed distributions. For scale-free networks, the scaling exponent is determined solely by the degree exponent of the network, independently of the control parameter. In contrast, on the Farey graph, a deterministic hierarchical small-world network, the scaling exponent varies continuously with the control parameter.

items.title: A Scalable Nonsuperconducting Tunnel Junction Technology
authors: Juho Luomahaara, Kristupas Razas, Omid Sharifi Sedeh, Renan P. Loreto, Janne S. Lehtinen, Mingchi Xu, Armel A. Cotten, Aldo Tarascio, Peter Müller, Nikolai Yurttagül, Lassi Lehtisyrjä, Leif Grönberg, Christian P. Scheller, Jonathan R. Prance, Michael D. Thompson, Richard P. Haley, Mika Prunnila, and Dominik M. Zumbühl
items.summary: Abstract Tunnel junctions are essential for various technologies ranging from classical microelectronics to quantum information and cryogenic electronics. Aluminum and its oxide (AlOx) have long dominated cryogenic and quantum tunnel junction applications for their excellent material quality and superconductivity. However, some applications require junctions to remain normal conducting, either as standalone components or integrated with superconducting circuitry. Magnetic fields, impurity doping, or proximity effects can suppress superconductivity, but often pose challenges for scalability and integration. Here, we present a CMOS-compatible normal conducting tunnel junction platform using TiW alloy electrodes and AlOx tunnel barriers, achieving high yield and uniformity through wafer-scale fabrication. As a cryogenic use-case, the wafers incorporate junction arrays designed for Coulomb blockade thermometry, confirming reliable normal conducting state performance down to 20 mK. These results demonstrate a scalable and integrable normal conducting junction technology, supporting its use in cryogenic, quantum, and nanoelectronic systems, including hybrid superconducting-normal metal circuits.

items.title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization of Composite Functions for Image-Based Inverse Problems in Materials Characterization
items.summary: Estimating physical parameters from scientific images is a common inverse problem in materials characterization that often relies on expensive physics-based simulations. In electron microscopy, specimen thickness and crystal mistilt are critical parameters that govern how electrons scatter through the sample, and therefore the accuracy of any atomic-scale structure recovered from it. They are commonly inferred by matching experimental position-averaged convergent-beam electron diffraction (PACBED) patterns to simulated ones, but grid searches scale poorly and neural-network methods require extensive pretraining that may not transfer to new conditions. Here, we propose scalable Bayesian optimization of composite functions (SBOCF), a simulation-efficient method that exploits the known composite structure of the image-matching objective and the intermediate information contained in simulated images. By representing PACBED images with patch-level summaries and two correction terms, SBOCF preserves the original pixel-wise objective while reducing the number of modeled outputs from 24,649 to 11. Under a budget of 50 simulator evaluations, SBOCF outperformed standard Bayesian optimization with expected improvement on synthetic SrTiO3 benchmarks with thick and thin specimens, reducing the median final SSE by up to 290 times in the thick-sample case. On experimental data, SBOCF produced parameter estimates consistent with previously reported values without task-specific pretraining. For a simulated mistilted specimen, using the SBOCF estimates in a downstream ptychographic reconstruction recovered sharp atoms that were otherwise blurred. These results establish SBOCF as a promising approach for inverse problems involving expensive simulators and high-dimensional structured outputs.

items.title: Stochastic evolution of interacting directed strings
items.summary: We study the stochastic dynamics of a system of $N$ polymer rings on an infinite cylinder with only excluded volume interaction, using simulations and also analytically. The strings can diffuse in the transverse direction by local Rouse-like moves where an up-kink changes to a down -kink, or vice versa. The motion is biased if the rates of flip are not equal. In the initial state, we start with a step initial condition: all the sites with a positive $y$ coordinate are empty, and the sites with $y \leq 0$ are occupied with a uniform density. We study the scaling form of the density profile in the hydrodynamic limit. The scaling form is a function of $y/\sqrt{t}$ in the unbiased case, and a function of $y/t$ in the biased case. In the unbiased case, in the steady state on a torus, the marginal probability distribution of the positions of the strings on a line with fixed $x$-coordinate is exactly same as that in the ground state of quantum-mechanical spin-less fermions on a line. The biased problem is equivalent to a growing surface in $2+1$ dimension, which is expected to be in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class.

items.title: Correction to “Physical- and Chemical-Dually ROS-Responsive Nano-in-Gel Platforms with Sequential Release of OX40 Agonist and PD-1 Inhibitor for Augmented Combination Immunotherapy”
authors: Yu Fu, Yulan Huang, Pingrong Li, Luyao Wang, Zhongjie Tang, Xinlong Liu, Xufei Bian, Shuang Wu, Xiaoyou Wang, Biyue Zhu, Yang Yu, Jiayun Jiang, and Chong Li
items.summary: National Natural Science Foundation of China10.13039/50110000180982204281

items.title: How anion composition governs structural frameworks and Li-ion transport in oxychloride solid-state electrolytes
items.summary: Mixed-anion lithium oxychlorides exhibit high Li conductivity, but the relationship between oxygen content, structural framework, and Li-ion transport remains unclear. Here, crystal structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials are used to examine $\mathrm{Li}_yM\mathrm{O}_x\mathrm{Cl}_{6-2x}$ ($M$ = Nb and Ta [Group 5] and $M$ = Ti, Zr, and Hf [Group 4]). Increasing oxygen content changes isolated chloride-rich polyhedra into one-dimensional chains and subsequently more highly connected two- and three-dimensional frameworks. In the Group 5 series, fast Li diffusion occurs over $x \approx 0.67$--1.5, where the Li sites form a three-dimensional percolating network. Potential of mean force maps and nudged elastic band calculations reveal that fast Li-ion transport requires a low-dimensional framework supporting long-range migration through undercoordinated Li sites with low barriers, together with similar energies across Li sites. Finally, we perform fine-grid compositional search, which identifies $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{0.67}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.67}$, $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{0.75}\mathrm{Cl}_{4.5}$, $\mathrm{LiNbO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$, and $\mathrm{LiTaO}_{1.5}\mathrm{Cl}_3$ as stable candidates with predicted room-temperature self-diffusivities of up to $\sim 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{cm}^2/\mathrm{s}$. These findings establish how oxygen content controls framework and Li-ion transport, guiding the design of lithium oxyhalide electrolytes.

items.title: Dynamic Pseudogap Model
items.summary: We formulate a theory of pseudogap formation generated by dynamic finite nesting vector ${\bf Q}$ fluctuations with characteristic oscillation frequency $ω_0$, and damping $γ$. Starting from a Hamiltonian describing electrons coupled to a classical Gaussian random field, we introduce the double - series representations of the single - particle Green's function within an Abelian (commuting) approximation to the exact SU(2) time evolution of the pseudogap problem. The resulting propagator naturally acquires a generalized Bogoliubov structure in which every stochastic scattering history is characterized by an effective dynamic gap, leading to a coherent superposition of dynamically broadened sidebands with complex Poisson weights. A central result of the theory is the emergence of a dynamically generated decoherence scale $Γ_{\rm eff}$ governing the crossover between two qualitatively different pseudogap regimes. For $ω_0>Γ_{\rm eff}$ the fluctuating field is resolved coherently and the double-series representation provides a controlled description of dynamic sideband formation. Conversely, when $Γ_{\rm eff}\gtrsimω_0$, coherence is progressively lost and the theory crosses over to the quasistatic fluctuating - gap regime described by the exact continued-fraction solution. The coherent and quasistatic descriptions are therefore interpreted as two complementary asymptotic limits of the same microscopic dynamic pseudogap model. The detailed results of numerical calculations for electron spectral density and density of states supporting our approach are presented for different sets of model parameters confirming the general picture of this crossover.

items.title: Topological flat bands from nonlinear periodic motion
items.summary: We use the Lax formulation of classical integrable systems to characterize the topology of nonlinear periodic orbits. For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom, we express the chiral-symmetric Lax operator along a periodic orbit in a frequency basis. Energy conservation makes both bands of the resulting tight-binding model exactly flat. The harmonic oscillator corresponds to a fully dimerized topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, while nonlinearity generates long-range hopping through higher harmonics. In the symmetric double well, the winding number changes as intrawell periodic orbits give way to an orbit spanning both wells, and the zero-energy edge mode of the semi-infinite chain disappears. We derive the edge-mode profile and show that its localization length diverges logarithmically as the separatrix is approached. At the separatrix, the period and the hopping decay length diverge while the band gap remains finite; this singular limit of the periodic motion allows the winding number of the infinite frequency chain to change. Canonical quantization of the Lax operator also connects the chiral winding numbers to supersymmetric quantum mechanics: for a bound system on the real line with simple turning points, their sum over all periodic orbits at a common positive energy equals the Witten index. We also apply the construction to periodic nonlinear waves through traveling-wave reductions. The finite-period winding number becomes undefined in their solitary-wave limits.

items.title: Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO$_2$ heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch
items.summary: RuO$_2$, once the flagship altermagnetic candidate, is now believed to be nonmagnetic in the bulk, yet weak, static and spatially inhomogeneous magnetism emerges at its surfaces and interfaces. Where this magnetism resides, what stabilises it, and whether it is connected to these states remain open questions. Here we address these questions at the Nb/RuO$_2$ interface using a superconducting spin switch. A GdN/Nb/RuO$_2$ trilayer allows interfacial exchange-field alignment to tune the superconducting transition temperature of Nb, probing interfacial magnetism inaccessible to conventional magnetometry. The switch reveals a hidden magnetic subsystem, which we attribute to a thin RuO$_x$ redox layer formed as Nb scavenges oxygen from RuO$_2$. This layer behaves as a weak and magnetically hard ferromagnet with vacancy-induced anisotropy. Furthermore, supercurrent amplifies the switching efficiency, making the probe sensitivity tunable in situ. Superconducting spin switches thus emerge as a quantitative low-temperature probe of hidden magnetism at buried interfaces.

items.title: Pair localization in one-dimensional quasicrystals with spin-dependent hopping
items.summary: We investigate the quantum localization of two interacting particles moving in a one-dimensional quasicrystal with unequal hopping amplitudes. Using a two-body Green's function approach, we determine the localization phase diagram of attractively and repulsively bound pairs, showing that increasing the hopping amplitude of one constituent while keeping the other fixed raises the critical quasiperiodic strength, promoting pair delocalization. The localization threshold nevertheless remains bounded above by the Aubry-André critical point of the slower constituent. Effective analytical descriptions capture pair localization in the limits of strong hopping imbalance and strong interactions. The dynamics of an initially on-site pair provides signatures of delocalization induced by unequal hopping amplitudes. In particular, the effective spreading exponent of the root-mean-square width of a pair distribution reveals a progression from localized to subdiffusive and eventually superdiffusive behavior as the hopping ratio increases. Our results establish unequal hopping amplitudes as a means of tuning the transport properties of interacting pairs in quasiperiodic lattices, with direct relevance to ultracold atoms in optical lattices.

items.title: Field-induced magnetic quantum phase transitions in a bilayer triangular lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$
items.summary: We present a $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study on the spin-$1/2$ bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnet K$_2$Co$_2$(HPO$_3$)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)(H$_2$O)$_2$. Measurements were performed at temperatures down to 0.06 K and magnetic fields up to 26 T. In the field range of 0.5 T to 4 T, the low-temperature spin-lattice relaxation rate $1/T_1$ exhibits a peak, signaling the onset of a magnetically ordered state. Within this ordered phase, $1/T_1$ shows gapless behavior, suggesting a spin supersolid phase. This ordering is suppressed around 4 T. Between 6 T and 18 T, clear splittings of the NMR spectra are observed, indicating the emergence of a second ordered magnetic phase. The field derivative of the low-temperature Knight shift $K_{\rm n}$ reveals changes in slope at approximately 10 T, 15.5 T, and 18 T. The first two features correspond to bulk magnetizations of $1/3$ and $2/3$ of the fully saturated moment, respectively, while the last one marks a quantum phase transition from the second ordered phase to the fully polarized state. These results establish the studied compound as a platform for investigating field-induced quantum phase transitions and emergent phases in frustrated bilayer triangular-lattice antiferromagnets.

items.title: A new representation of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic potentials through stochastic duality
items.summary: We revisit the classical problem of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic force fields by combining homogenization with stochastic duality. We consider a specific class of fluctuations in which the internal state of the force field is independently redrawn from a fixed distribution at Poisson-distributed times. In the homogenization framework, the effective diffusion coefficient \(D_{\rm eff}\) is expressed in terms of a corrector function satisfying a backward Kolmogorov equation. For the redraw dynamics considered here, the equation governing the spatial derivative of the corrector can be reinterpreted as the stationary forward equation of a dual system obtained by reversing the force field, \(F\to-F\). This relation eliminates the corrector and yields a representation of \(D_{\rm eff}\) entirely in terms of stationary densities and probability currents of the physical and dual systems. We further introduce an auxiliary function \(Q(x)\) whose spatial variation is determined by the stationary current. When this current vanishes, \(Q(x)\) becomes independent of position and the effective diffusion coefficient reduces to the local relation \( D_{\rm eff}=L^2Q. \) This result generalizes the classical Lifson--Jackson relation to fluctuating periodic force fields. We verify the theory using analytical calculations, numerical solutions of the stationary equations, and direct simulations of the long-time particle displacement, including a driven system with nonzero stationary current.

items.title: Three-body corrections to the Brownian viscosity of hard spheres without hydrodynamic interactions
items.summary: For Brownian hard spheres without hydrodynamic interactions, we study the part of the contact stress produced by three-body correlations: the third-order coefficient of the zero-shear Brownian viscosity. Kirkwood superposition gives zero for this coefficient: three nonzero pair contributions cancel exactly. An elementary radial identity exposes the cancellation, and evaluating closures with the same contact stress makes their coefficients directly comparable. Although superposition solves the bulk equation, it leaves a flux error on each shared contact. This error defines a unique finite-energy weak correction whose positive diffusive dissipation, suitably normalized, is a weak-energy coefficient. Explicit symmetric trials yield a variational lower bound and a residual upper bound, and exact integration with outward rational arithmetic proves that the weak-energy coefficient lies between 1.8266948 and 1.8267157. For the physical viscosity coefficient this is a conditional interval: the two coefficients coincide when the physical three-body correction equals the weak correction and the remote remainder of the pair adjoint identity, a surface term at large pair separation, vanishes. The interval excludes every closure coefficient compared here, including the zero of superposition. Hydrodynamic interactions contribute at the same orders in real suspensions, where rheometry measures total viscosities, so the coefficient is a quantitative benchmark for theories and simulations of dilute three-body Brownian stress in this model.

items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.summary: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for the decoherence of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations in which the spins outside each cluster keep exchanging spin projections in pairs reproduce the measured Hahn-echo coherence time of NV$^-$ centres in a substitutional-nitrogen bath to within 12%, inside the statistical uncertainty. Driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters, the same calculation inverts the attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.0-6.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies at 1 ppm, and 2.2-6.5 times longer from 0.01 to 10 ppm. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts those frequencies. Were every defect on the same crystallographic site, all would shift alike and still match, and the splitting would gain little, a factor 1.2. Real defects occupy symmetry-equivalent sites pointing in different directions, so neighbours land at different frequencies and stop exchanging: a factor 2.3. What governs the coherence time is therefore the fraction of bath pairs sharing a transition frequency, not the size of the zero-field splitting. Vacancy aggregation extends NV$^-$ spin coherence rather than shortening it.

items.title: Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators
items.summary: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect is usually realized through ferromagnetism or magnetic dop ing, which limits material choices and often results in low mobility, disorder sensitivity, and low operating temperatures. Here, we propose a mechanism to achieve the QAH phase without net magnetization, using altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator (WTI). The altermagnetic order selectively gaps the Dirac cone at the Z point, while hybridization between the top and bottom surfaces of the WTI thin film opens a trivial gap at the point, generating a Chern number C = 1 phase with a single chiral edge channel. We verify the topological transition through both a minimal thin-film model and a slab geometry, and compute the associated Hall response. As altermagnets and layered WTIs already exist experimentally, this mechanism offers a promising and experimentally accessible route to realizing QAH phases without magnetic doping or global magnetization. The results indicate that altermagnetic surface engineering may provide a clean and controllable pathway for realizing dissipationless edge transport in layered quantum materials.

items.title: Facilitated Relaxation Overrides Energetic Pathways in a Multiphase Square-Kagome Artificial Spin Ice
items.summary: Relaxation in interacting many-body systems is typically assumed to follow energy minimization, yet local dynamical rules can determine which microscopic pathways are accessible. In facilitated relaxation, these pathways are enabled or blocked by neighboring configurations. However, isolating such rules in natural materials is difficult because energetics, disorder and dynamics are usually entangled. Here we realize a geometrically tunable square-kagome artificial spin ice-a lithographic nanomagnet array-that provides a clean, designable platform for facilitated relaxation. The array hosts two tunable nearest-neighbor interactions and supports multiple low-energy phases: spin crystal, spin liquid and spin foam. In the spin-foam phase, abundant facilitator configurations allow relaxation to follow Boltzmann statistics. In the spin-crystal phase, by contrast, domain-wall excitations are trapped in non-Boltzmann distributions, although energetically preferred relaxation channels exist. The ordered crystal background lacks the facilitators needed to connect topologically distinct domain-wall classes. These classes are therefore kinetically isolated, as observed in both experiment and Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that transition-network topology can override energetic relaxation, establishing artificial spin ice as a programmable platform for constrained dynamics and nonergodic relaxation.

items.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
items.summary: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime, by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$), outperforming the conventional semiconductor such as InAs. Furthermore, we propose universal material design recipes: strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive materials-discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.

items.title: FrOGS: Discrete Neural Sampler for Independent Alloy Configurations Across Chemical Conditions
items.summary: Predicting the thermodynamic properties of an alloy requires sampling its configurations across many chemical conditions and recovering free energies on a common absolute scale. Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) is the standard tool, but it requires separate simulations at different conditions, and auxiliary free-energy methods such as thermodynamic integration are used to place results on a common absolute scale. Modern discrete neural samplers typically use reverse KL divergence as the objective and can be mode-seeking or biased. We present Free energy Offering Generative Sampler (FrOGS), a hybrid discrete neural sampler that couples an autoregressive model to a continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) to be trained jointly under a single shared loss. FrOGS draws i.i.d. configurations, returns an unbiased estimate of the partition function, and gives consistent estimates of thermodynamic observables. We train a single model across a wide range of chemical conditions to produce estimates on a common absolute free-energy scale. FrOGS matches exact finite-size results on the 2D Ising model and reference phase diagrams for AgPd and CuAu, without mode collapse. We additionally compare to SEGAL, a published autoregressive baseline, and find that only FrOGS recovers the stability range of the CuAu$_3$ phase.

items.title: Rare-earth oxysulfides RE$_2$O$_2$S as model mixed-anion frustrated magnets
items.summary: The study of low-dimensional and anisotropic magnetism is a promising avenue for the discovery of novel quantum phenomena. Mixed-anion materials, defined by the coordination of metal cations by two or more distinct anionic species, provide an intrinsically anisotropic platform for the tuning of structural, magnetic, and electronic properties. In this work, we report the synthesis and characterization of a family of rare-earth oxysulfide (RE$_2$O$_2$S) antiferromagnets (AFM) possessing a triangular-bilayer slab lattice geometry. Transitions consistent with long-range AFM order are observed for the majority of compositions, with several (RE = Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm) having been previously unreported. Although assumed to form stoichiometrically, pair distribution function (PDF) analysis provides evidence for significant, synthesis-dependent interslab structural disorder as RE$_2$O$_{2+x}$S$_{1-x}$, resulting in significant variability in the bulk magnetic response of the Nd member. This work highlights the tunability of frustrated magnetic ground states in rare-earth-based mixed-anion materials, and the importance of thorough structural characterization in the discovery of new mixed-anion magnets.

items.title: Anomalous Localization and Mobility Edges in Non-Hermitian Quasicrystals with Disordered Imaginary Gauge Fields
items.summary: How localization emerges in open wave systems can differ fundamentally from the familiar picture in closed materials. Here we show that a quasiperiodic chain with spatially disordered non-reciprocal couplings supports a form of localization in which the relevant boundary does not separate spreading and trapped waves, but two different kinds of confinement. One regime shows erratic skin accumulation at disorder-selected positions inside the lattice, whereas the other shows conventional Anderson localization with centers distributed across the system. Adding longer-range hopping turns this transition into an anomalous mobility edge between these two localized sectors. We identify the transition using real-space profiles, Lyapunov exponents, spectral winding, and wave-packet evolution. For individual disorder realizations, wave packets drift in a direction fixed by spectral topology, while averaging over disorder cancels opposite drifts and restores conventional transport. These results provide experimentally accessible signatures of anomalous localization in engineered open systems.

items.title: Geometry-Selective Higher-order topological insulators induced by $d_{xy}$ altermagnet
items.summary: We show that proximity to a $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnet provides an effective route to engineering boundary-geometry-dependent higher-order topological phases. The boundary geometry plays a crucial role in determining the topological properties: axis-aligned edge states remain gapless, whereas diagonal edges acquire effective masses with alternating signs, giving rise to four corner modes localized at the mass domain walls. By projecting onto the edge-state subspace, we derive the effective edge Hamiltonians for different boundary geometries. Furthermore, $π$-flux defects introduced under periodic boundary conditions yield zero-energy bound states localized at the flux cores, providing complementary evidence for nontrivial topology without physical boundaries. The interplay between the Zeeman field and the altermagnetic order drives a topological transition through the closing and reopening of the edge gap, while the bulk gap remains open. These findings highlight the crucial role of boundary geometry in higher-order topology and establish proximity-induced $d_{xy}$-wave altermagnetism as a route to engineering higher-order topological phases.

items.title: Direct Visualization of Na,K-ATPase Clustering by 3D DNA-PAINT MINFLUX Nanoscopy
authors: Bruno Stojcic, Ana Agostinho, Luca Panconi, Hans Blom, and Hjalmar Brismar
items.summary: Abstract The sodium–potassium pump (Na,K-ATPase) is an essential plasma-membrane transporter that consumes 20%–30% of cellular energy, and up to approximately 50% in the kidneys. Whether it assembles into defined oligomers in its native membrane has been debated for decades. Resolving this question demands imaging precision at molecular length scales. Here, we combine 3D MINFLUX nanoscopy with DNA-PAINT to map EGFP-tagged Na,K-ATPase α1 and β1 subunits in mammalian cells with 3–5 nm localization precision. We introduce two point-cloud analysis tools: a data-driven algorithm that assigns localizations to the apical or basal membrane, removing trans-membrane artifacts, and a sequential nearest-neighbor analysis that estimates oligomer stoichiometry without structural priors. Both subunits show preferential nearest-neighbor distances of approximately 7 nm, direct evidence of dimerization, and are further organized into nanoclusters of approximately 7 to 12 molecules. These results provide direct structural evidence of Na,K-ATPase self-assembly and a framework for quantifying membrane-protein clustering at single-molecule resolution.

items.title: 2D quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation driven by highly-bichromatic fields
authors: Xiaozhou Zou, Lucie Jurkovičová, Anne Weber, Cong Zhao, Martin Albrecht, Ondřej Finke, Alexandr Vendl, Annika Grenfell, Wojciech Szuba, Jaroslav Nejdl, Eric Constant, Margarita Khokhlova, Emilio Pisanty, Ondřej Hort and Amelle Zaïr
items.summary: We experimentally observe a new type of quantum-path interference, in two-dimensions (2D-QPI), in high-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by an orthogonally-polarised highly-bichromatic field. This regime is characterised by a relatively strong orthogonal second-harmonic component beyond the weak perturbation limit, such that the electron dynamics are substantially modified. In this highly-bichromatic regime, we demonstrate that 2D-QPI is encoded in the measured harmonic intensity modulations with respect to the relative phase of the two-colour field. The modulations of the odd-order harmonics show a monomodal behaviour, whereas the even harmonics are modulated in a bimodal structure. Our calculations using the strong-field approximation and saddle-point method disentangle contributions from multiple quantum orbits in this HHG regime, revealing that the dipole response for both odd and even harmonics inherits the dynamic symmetry of the orthogonally-polarised driving field. This new type of 2D-QPI offers a novel route to HHG spectroscopy of attosecond electron dynamics by lifting up the dimensionality of the quantum paths involved in the interference.

items.title: Coherent receiver for continuous-variable quantum key distribution using a 3 × 3 beam splitter and single-ended photodetectors
authors: Pol Adillon, Samael Sarmiento, Jeison Tabares, Hugues de Riedmatten and Sebastian Etcheverry
items.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (QKD) relies on coherent detection. Conventional coherent receivers typically use an optical 90° hybrid and two balanced photodetectors providing robust phase-diversity detection. Here, we introduce and characterize a simplified receiver architecture based on a symmetric 3 × 3 beam splitter (BS) and three single-ended photodetectors for continuous-variable QKD. Results demonstrate that the 3 × 3 BS-based architecture provides similar performance to conventional ones while reducing optical-hardware complexity.

items.title: Magnon-mediated cooling by heating in a spin-selective quantum dot system
items.summary: We demonstrate how nonequilibrium magnons can drive the cooling by heating effect in a spin-selective quantum dot system. The mechanism relies on magnon-assisted spin-flip transitions that transfer electrons between two ferromagnetic electrodes maintained at different temperatures, with the magnetic insulator acting as the high-temperature energy source. In the limit of fully spin-polarized antiparallel electrodes, the transport enters a tight-coupling regime in which each absorbed magnon is accompanied by the transfer of a single electron. This one-to-one correspondence directly links the cooling power to the heat supplied by the magnonic reservoir and enables the thermodynamic performance to approach its upper bound. We further show how finite spin polarization introduces parasitic spin channels that suppress cooling and reduce the operating range. An extended dual quantum dot configuration restores cooling by heating without net charge current and enhances the cooling power. Our results establish magnons as a distinct microscopic energy carrier for cooling by heating and provide a route toward its realization in solid-state spin-caloritronic systems.

items.title: Particle dynamics in constant synthetic non-abelian fields: I. the classical treatment
authors: Subramanya Bhat K N, Amita Das, Bhooshan Paradkar and V Ravishankar
items.summary: Yang–Mills (YM) theory has evolved beyond its origins in the strong interaction to become an effective framework for condensed matter, ultracold atomic, and photonic systems, where synthetic non-Abelian gauge fields enable phenomena such as spin transport, the spin-Hall effect, and polarization control. These systems provide access to gauge-field dynamics beyond the reach of high-energy experiments. In all the above mentioned cases, the state of the system evolves in an effective external YM field. Here, we report the results of a classical study (as preparatory for a full quantum study) of particle dynamics in constant gauge fields produced by constant gauge potentials, by focusing on configurations that are experimentally relevant. We show that consequences such as unbounded trajectories in a constant color magnetic field and unusual correlation between charge and color dynamics have a direct bearing on the physical phenomena observed, especially in experiments involving charge and spin transports. More generally, this work also shows how the low energy systems can act as laboratories to probe quintessentially non-Abelian features such as the Wu-Yang ambiguity.

items.title: Observing quantum-classical correspondence through optical path integrals
authors: Li-Man Tian, Yunfei Wang, Ying Zhou, Chang Li, Shanchao Zhang, Xuan Dai, Bai-Chuan Long, Hui Yan, Shi-Liang Zhu and Yong-Li Wen
items.summary: The quantum–classical correspondence (QCC) describes how quantum systems recover classical behavior in the semiclassical limit. One of the crucial mechanisms to this correspondence is the concept of action, which governs dynamics in both classical mechanics and quantum path integrals. Despite its fundamental importance, experimental access to the action of individual quantum paths remains crucial yet challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a method to measure the action of quantum paths between fixed spacetime points, based on weak-value measurement techniques. By introducing and analyzing the spectrum of the norm of the action gradient, we identify not only single but also multiple stationary-action paths in systems exhibiting complex QCC. Using an optical setup that simulates photon propagation in free space and under an impulsive potential, we reconstruct pathwise actions and observe sharp dips in the spectrum that correspond precisely to classical trajectories. This work provides a framework for directly accessing and analyzing the action, opening new avenues for experimentally exploring the QCC.

items.title: Algebraic structures of the Lindblad equation
authors: Leonel Bixano, Guillermo López-Alvarez, Victor Alberto Cruz-Barriguete, Víctor Guadalupe Ibarra-Sierra, José Luis Cardoso, Juan Carlos Sandoval-Santana and Alejandro Kunold
items.summary: We investigate the algebraic structure underlying the Lindblad equation for finite-dimensional open quantum systems. Using an orthonormal Hermitian operator basis, we represent the Liouville superoperator in a model-independent basis of Hermitian superoperators realizing the standard left–right multiplication maps. We express their multiplication, commutator, and anticommutator relations explicitly in terms of the Lie and Jordan structure constants of the underlying operator basis. This formulation makes explicit how dissipative contributions can extend the generator beyond the adjoint Lie algebra associated with purely Hamiltonian evolution. The multiplication rules allow us to derive differential equations for the expansion coefficients of the dynamical map. We further derive recursion relations for the iterative construction of the algebra in multiqubit systems. For a fixed operator basis, the algebraic data can be precomputed and reused, while the Hamiltonian and dissipative parameters enter through a single set of coefficients. Computational benchmarks compare memory usage and construction time for algebraic, direct, and standard Kronecker implementations. For the cases tested, the algebraic implementation reduces peak memory requirements and construction time relative to the direct implementation. In the benchmarks, the standard Kronecker implementation requires less memory and time than both alternatives and enables calculations for larger numbers of qubits. These findings establish the computational limitations of the present algebraic implementation alongside its explicit characterization of the underlying superoperator algebra. An accompanying Mathematica notebook provides five examples covering algebraic verification for one-, two-, and three-qubit operator bases and numerical transmon dynamics. The examples confirm agreement with the direct method, illustrate an approximate gate and population leakage beyond the computational subspace, and use Choi matrices to check Hermiticity preservation, complete positivity, and trace preservation.

items.title: Experiment-Compatible Measurement–Feedback Quantum State Preparation with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Xiaotian Nie, 晓天 聂, Tao Zhang, 韬 张, Linghui Chen and 凌辉 陈
items.summary: Ground-state preparation is a critical task in quantum simulation and quantum computing, as it enables the study of correlated phases and the generation of entangled resource states. While measurement–feedback control has emerged as a promising route to state preparation, existing schemes either rely on handcrafted, task-specific policies or are designed using full quantum-state information that is unavailable in real experiments and becomes impractical for large many-body systems. Here we develop an adaptive measurement–feedback protocol based on reinforcement learning under partial observability. The controller uses only the history of experimentally accessible measurement outcomes to choose both the measurement operator and the feedback action in real time. To make training compatible with experiments, we introduce a stochastic terminal reward built from one-shot measurements of randomly sampled Hamiltonian components, avoiding unphysical full-state reconstruction while remaining an unbiased estimator of the target energy. We demonstrate the method by preparing ground states of the Bose–Hubbard model and by generating GHZ states, establishing a scalable and hardware-compatible route to quantum state preparation.

items.title: Electron–Phonon Coupling with Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Transfer
items.summary: Spin and orbital angular momentum transfer between lattice vibrations and electrons has become an important focus beyond traditional electron–phonon coupling. Recent studies of spin–rotation coupling have shown that the rotational motion of lattice elastic vibrations can directly interact with the electron spin. Here we develop a microscopic description of the electron–phonon angular momentum coupling beyond spin–rotation coupling, which includes both the electron spin and orbital angular momentum from the relative motion of atoms in a local co-rotating lattice. We relate the lattice angular velocity to the atom-relative angular momentum through the inertia tensor, so that the lattice angular momentum, coupled to total electron angular momentum, contains both phonon spin and orbital angular momentum. The microscopic construction connects with continuum rotation descriptions, extends to non-rigid motion, and reveals discrete-lattice effects beyond the long-wavelength limit. These results provide a microscopic framework of electron–phonon coupling with spin and orbital angular momentum transfer, enabling both studies of phonon-driven electron spin and orbital dynamics and electron-driven phonon spin and orbital dynamics.

items.title: Circular Phonon Dichroism in d-Wave Altermagnets
authors: Ding Li, 顶 李, Tao Qin, 涛 秦, Jianhui Zhou and 建辉 周
items.summary: Altermagnets, a new class of collinear antiferromagnets, exhibit momentum-dependent spin splitting and offer compelling advantages for antiferromagnetic spintronics. However, the magnetic order is intrinsically difficult to read out, which hinders practical applications. We propose finite-momentum circular phonon dichroism (CPD) as a direct probe that distinguishes the two opposite out-of-plane Néel vector configurations in two-dimensional d-wave altermagnets. Combining Onsager reciprocity with C2z lattice symmetry, we find that the dichroic signal reverses sign when the Néel vector is flipped for the in-plane phonon wave vectors. Moreover, a channel-resolved decomposition identifies the CPD originates from the interband coherent transitions. Representative finite-momentum cuts show pronounced dichroic asymmetric ratio, with |ηCPD| = 36%. Our work reveals that the circular-ultrasound absorption can distinguish the two opposite out-of-plane Néel vector configurations of d-wave altermagnets.

items.title: 4f-multiplet-enabled electron–phonon decoupling towards high thermoelectric performance in rare-earth topological semimetal TbPtBi
items.summary: Abstract Topological materials exhibit strong magneto-thermoelectric effects owing to the ultrahigh mobility of electrons, yet bosonic phonon transport typically remains insensitive to magnetic fields. Crystal electric fields (CEF) combined with Zeeman splitting in rare-earth ions yielding discrete 4 f excitation levels can in principle but have rarely been demonstrated to reduce phonon thermal conductivity by resonant phonon scattering. Therefore, rare-earth topological semimetals offer a unique platform in which electrical and phononic thermal transport can be intrinsically decoupled by magnetic fields. Herein, taking TbPtBi as an example, we demonstrate pronounced electron–phonon decoupling enabled by field-tunable 4 f multiplets. High-mobility topological carriers give rise to high magneto-thermopowers and thermoelectric power factors. Meanwhile, multi-resonant phonon scattering by Zeeman-split Tb 3+ CEF levels suppresses the phonon thermal conductivity, leading to a complete quenching of the phonon peak and a reduction of nearly 90% at 13 K by applying a magnetic field of ∼9 T. Theoretical calculations indicate a redistribution of phonon lifetimes that can drive the lattice into a phonon-glass-like state. These results establish 4 f -multiplet engineering as a new way for electron-phonon decoupling and demonstrate the great potential of rare-earth topological materials for exceptional magneto-thermoelectric performance.

items.title: Conformational inversion mediated organic crystal actuator with extended stroke, self-healing, and optical switching
items.summary: Abstract Dynamic molecular crystals with the capability to effectively convert thermal energy into mechanical work offer a compelling platform for microactuators. However, developing crystalline actuation materials that simultaneously achieve large and reversible deformation, rapid response, robust cyclability, and integrated optoelectronic functionality remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we take advantage of the conformational inversion of cyclohexyl groups and have rationally developed a dynamic organic crystal based on a dibenzothiophene sulfone derivative, BcDT, which exhibits exceptionally large, rapid, and reversible elongation. The thermally induced chair-to-boat conformational inversion of the introduced cyclohexyl moieties drives a cooperative phase transition that yields a linear elongation of ~14.3% along the crystal long axis, which delivers a work density of ~6.8 × 10 2 J m −3 and an efficiency of ~0.014%. Notably, the crystal features an uncommon self-healing capability, autonomously repairing macroscopic cracks during heating/cooling stages, ensuring its structural integrity and reliable actuation over multiple thermal cycles. The phase transition also enables reversible switching of linear and nonlinear optical properties, including a 4.2-fold modulation of two-photon excited fluorescence and tunable polarization anisotropy. Leveraging these properties, we demonstrate that BcDT crystals can function as microactuator devices to propel a heavy object and cooperatively lift a platform. This work establishes a molecular design strategy that integrates rapid, high-stroke actuation, self-healing, and optical switching within a single crystalline system, overcoming key functional limitations of current microactuators based on dynamic molecular crystals.

items.title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
items.summary: Abstract Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores (or channels) and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specifically, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places a limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are, however, difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and, crucially, exhibits long endurance, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with exceptionally high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced by the effective processing of largescale and event-based information in the identification of both grayscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport, in addition to the well-documented pore’s charge and size, and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

items.title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
items.summary: Abstract The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO 2 , which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH 4 conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h −1 , a high C 2 hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g −1 h −1 and 90.1% C 2 selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O 2 /CH 4 reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C 2 H 6 product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

items.title: Beyond acceptor emissivity: interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder regulate nonradiative voltage losses for organic solar cells
items.summary: Abstract Suppressing non-radiative energy loss (Δ E nr ) is critical for achieving high open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet it remains unclear whether intrinsic emissive properties of acceptors can reliably predict voltage losses. Here, we report a counterintuitive phenomenon in which a low-emissive acceptor (D6) delivers a significantly reduced Δ E nr compared with the benchmark L8-BO when blended with D18. Despite lower intrinsic emissivity of D6, the D18: D6 system exhibits a markedly higher electroluminescence efficiency and a reduced Δ E nr of 0.153 eV, leading to an enhanced V OC of 0.980 V. Incorporation of D6 into the D18: L8-BO host yields a ternary device with a power conversion efficiency of 21.01%. Sensitive EQE analysis reveals that favorable CT-state energetics partially contribute to the reduced non-radiative loss of D18: D6, while temperature-dependent photoluminescence analysis further identifies suppressed interfacial dynamic disorder as a critical additional factor. While dynamic disorder is significantly increased in the D18: L8-BO blend, it is effectively suppressed in the D18: D6 system, resulting in preserved emissive interfacial states. Complementary structural and kinetic studies demonstrate that D6 modulates aggregation pathways and stabilizes nanoscale morphology, enabling efficient charge transport and reduced recombination. Furthermore, the beneficial role of D6 can be extended to multiple high-performance acceptor systems, demonstrating its general applicability as an interfacial regulator for improving photovoltaic performance. These results highlight that non-radiative voltage loss in OSCs is governed by the interplay between interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder rather than by the intrinsic emissivity of the acceptor alone, providing new insights into the design of low-energy-loss photovoltaic materials.

items.title: Back-end-of-line-integrated carbon nanotube modules for acceleration of silicon logic and clock networks
items.summary: Abstract Geometric transistor scaling no longer delivers proportional timing gains in advanced silicon logic integrated circuits (ICs), where operating frequency is increasingly bounded by high-capacitance, fanout-limited logic paths and clock networks. The emerging τ -scaling perspective reframes this limitation as a time-constant problem across the driver-interconnect-load system. Here we report τ Drive, a monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) carbon-nanotube (CNT) active timing overlay that selectively compresses the dominant τ of silicon logic and clock paths. Unlike topology-folding approaches that primarily shorten interconnects, τ Drive preserves the underlying silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) fabric and inserts back-end-of-line (BEOL) integrated CNT timing cells only at load-critical driver stages. A 180-nm Si/500-nm CNT experimental platform verifies low-temperature CNT-on-Si integration, and will enable CNT-assisted Si ring oscillators to achieve a 294% output-swing improvement and 30% effective-current enhancement with a fanout (FO) of 5. In simulations of a 3-nm Si central processing unit (CPU) using calibrated 10-nm CNT CMOS standard cells, selective CNT insertion reduces FO = 39 local delay and transition by 87.5% and 89.5%, respectively, and a single-cell replacement improves the full-CPU logic-path maximum frequency ( F max ) by 2.3%, while selective clock-tree enhancement raises the frequency bound from 2.85 to 2.93 GHz with only a 0.01 mW increase in clock-tree synthesis (CTS) power. These results establish CNT-on-Si M3D as a low-intrusion, vertically accessible drive resource for post-geometric τ compression, as well as a novel logic-folding approach.

items.title: Faster global mid-depth ocean connectivity in observations
items.summary: Abstract Ocean circulation redistributes heat, carbon, and biogeochemical tracers through transport pathways connecting distant ocean regions, yet global connectivity of mid-depth transport pathways remains poorly constrained by observations. Here we establish an observational benchmark of global mid-depth water-mass connectivity, using more than 1.3 million displacements recorded by 9,920 Argo floats over the past two decades. The benchmark reveals that observed connectivity is generally faster than simulated, with mean connectivity timescales 23-29% shorter in the real ocean. This systematic discrepancy between observed and simulated mid-depth ocean connectivity arises from overestimated turnover timescales within subtropical gyre interiors and underrepresentation of rapid inter-basin exchanges along equatorial and western boundary pathways in the simulation-derived networks, particularly in the South Pacific and South Atlantic. These findings provide quantitative constraints on ocean interior transport, with broad implications for estimates of climate memory, tracer age, carbon sequestration, and marine biogeographic connectivity.

items.title: Revisiting the multi-mode rhombus circuit
authors: Pablo Aramburu Sanchez, Trevyn F.Q. Larson, Anthony P. McFadden, Constantin Schrade, Joshua Combes, András Gyenis
items.summary: Designing qubits with noise insensitivity represents an important direction to building fault-tolerant quantum computers because they can reduce the hardware overhead of quantum error correction schemes. Aramburu Sanchez et al. study a protected superconducting circuit, the rhombus qubit, and demonstrate its protection against certain errors. In addition, they determine the limitations of the protection in the rhombus through experimental and theoretical noise analysis.

items.title: Dimensional effect on ultrafast spin dynamics in vacancy-engineered ferromagnet Cr2−δTe2
authors: Yifan Ren, Zhou Wang, Qinwen Lu, Zhongzhu Jiang, Ruihuan Lan, Biwen Huang, Bolin Li, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Zhigao Sheng
items.summary: Ren et al. show that vacancy-engineered Cr2−δTe2 provides an ideal platform to reveal how magnetic dimensionality governs ultrafast spin dynamics. Reducing dimensionality strongly increases spin-wave frequency and damping, driven by enhanced magnetic anisotropy and magnon-vacancy scattering, respectively. Weakened interlayer exchange further suppresses out-of-plane spin-wave propagation, revealing how dimensional confinement reshapes both the local dynamics and transport of spin waves.

items.title: TASCopilot: A provenance-preserving assistant for triple-axis neutron scattering
items.summary: Experimental decisions often depend on evidence scattered across papers, instrument logs, data files, and specialist software. A scientific assistant must connect that evidence without turning a plausible interpretation into an unsupported conclusion. TAS Co-pilot addresses this problem for triple-axis spectroscopy (TAS), which uses neutrons to probe material structure and excitations. It preserves provenance: the sources, processing steps, and review decisions behind each result. Independently maintained scientific tools communicate through structured requests and results; validation rules and human review govern how evidence can support a claim. Language models extract information and explain outcomes but do not approve scientific claims or control the instrument. Dependency-aware reduction executes existing scientific routines and reuses unchanged intermediate results. A retrospective SrMn$_2$Sb$_2$ study connects literature on a related material and historical alignment records to modeling of magnetic excitations in 20 measured scans. A live BT-7 study uses a dedicated instrument interface for fine alignment and 40 adaptively selected measurements. Agreement with a conventional measurement of the same crystal at shared conditions supports the acquisition and analysis chain. These cases demonstrate a methodology for maintaining inspectable evidence across literature, numerical analysis, and measurement at a user facility.

items.title: Linear equivalence of nonlinear recurrent neural networks
items.summary: The covariance matrix of a large nonlinear recurrent neural network is shown to match that of a linear network with the same couplings, driven by independent noise, for typical random couplings with independent, identically distributed elements. This linear equivalence, previously proposed as an ansatz, is derived using a two-site cavity method and confirmed in simulations. With zero mean activities, and with sign-flip symmetry when units repeat, weak correlations between units reduce even-order moments at leading order to products of single-site and two-site moments, recovering results first obtained diagrammatically. In models with nonzero mean activities, including a recurrent network with Hebbian plasticity and a saturating Lotka-Volterra model, the temporal means obey a self-consistent mean-field equation, and linear equivalence holds for the connected covariance matrix. Parts of this work were done in collaboration with AI models.

items.title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
items.summary: Van der Waals superatomic crystals represent an intriguing class of materials, exhibiting unique ultrafast electronic and structural responses arising from their hierarchical crystal structure. These materials bridge the properties of semiconductors, molecular solids, and nanocrystal arrays, hosting a range of many-body interactions that can be controlled with atomically precise structures. To establish the structure-function correlation, it is necessary to understand element-specific electronic states arising from complex superatomic unit cells. Here, we use transient XUV spectroscopy to individually probe the dynamics of photoexcited electrons and holes in Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$ superatomic crystals. We simultaneously measure photodynamics at the Re O$_{2}$ and Se M$_{4,5}$ edges, enabling decomposition of excited-state dynamics into the contributions of electron, hole, band gap, and phonon dynamics occurring around Re and Se atoms. By correlating spectral features at the Re and Se edges, we infer the existence of flat conduction bands and identify hot hole transfer from Re to Se atoms. We observe phonon oscillations driven by hole-mediated displacive excitations. The measurements highlight that the photodynamics are dominated by charge transfer between metallic sites which drives phonon coupling in the nonequilibrium state. This work provides insights into the optoelectronic applications of superatomic crystals for future tuning of emergent material properties.

items.title: A Perspective on Topological Charge Density Wave Materials
items.summary: Charge density waves are among the earliest known ordered states in quantum materials, yet they have re-emerged at the center of modern discussions of topology, symmetry breaking, and collective dynamics. In several material classes, charge-density-wave order reshapes electronic bands, boundary states, defect structures, and electromagnetic responses in ways that invite a topological interpretation. Real-space imaging has shown that incommensurate order can form networks of phase defects rather than uniform modulations. Boundary-resolved spectroscopy has revealed in-gap modes whose existence and spatial structure track the charge-density-wave order, although such observations remain confined to a single material family. In Weyl materials, density-wave gaps have been linked to axion-like magnetoelectric response, placing the charge-density-wave phase within a dynamical-field description of the effective action. In kagome metals, charge order is intertwined with Berry curvature, unconventional symmetry breaking, and superconductivity. These developments have led to the term "topological charge density wave," but the phrase describes several physically distinct phenomena. We distinguish three meanings: (i) topology of the order parameter and its defects, (ii) topology of the charge-density-wave-reconstructed electronic structure and its boundary modes, and (iii) axion-like electromagnetic response generated by density-wave order. The experimental and theoretical support for these three meanings differs substantially.
