These bounds are optimal in every dimension: the maximal nonzero-gap multiplicity has order $L^{d-1}$, and suitable many-body eigenstates realize matching variance lower bounds and show that the concentration bound cannot be improved in estimates uniform in the tolerance parameter.

items.title: Renewal Bias in Parallel Simulations of Absorbing Processes
items.summary: Asynchronous parallel simulations of stochastic processes with absorbing states can exhibit systematic sampling bias when trajectory durations depend on their eventual absorbing outcomes. Workers that continuously restart upon absorption preferentially record rapidly terminating trajectories within a fixed computational budget, distorting the observed ensemble statistics. We investigate this effect using a minimal renewal model with two absorbing states and state-dependent exponential durations. Renewal theory yields exact expressions for the expected number and composition of completed trajectories, showing that the resulting bias decreases algebraically with execution time but persists as the number of parallel workers increases at fixed budget. We compare continuous sampling with First-Trajectory Filtering, which retains only the initial trajectory attempted by each worker. Although finite execution deadlines introduce residual censoring bias, this bias decreases exponentially with the computational budget. An analytical mean-squared error calculation reveals budget-dependent crossover worker allocations beyond which First-Trajectory Filtering becomes more accurate despite collecting fewer trajectories. We also examine the limitations of statistical inference under severe censoring when the absorbing-state probabilities and characteristic durations are unknown. Finally, simulations of the Axelrod model near its nonequilibrium transition demonstrate the preferential sampling of rapidly absorbing fragmented configurations, illustrating the relevance of the renewal mechanism in a spatially interacting system. Our results show that increasing computational throughput does not necessarily improve statistical accuracy and highlight the importance of accounting for trajectory-duration heterogeneity in parallel simulations of absorbing processes.

items.title: Mean-Field Theory for the Three-State Active Lattice Gas Model
items.summary: We develop a mean-field description including spatial structure for a simplified version of the three-state active matter model studied by Venzel et al. (Phys. Rev. E 110, 014109 (2024)). The resulting triangular lattice of coupled nonlinear differential equations are integrated numerically using a fourth-order Runge-Kutta scheme. Starting from various ordered initial configurations, we probe the stability of the corresponding stationary states, revealing the presence of various high-density ordered structures in the density(\r{ho})-noise(η) plane. The results are compared with Monte Carlo simulations of the simplified model, yielding, in certain cases, unexpected transitions between ordered configuration types.

items.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
items.summary: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic $Γ$ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gapless Tomonaga-Luttinger-liquid (TLL) phase appears only in the isotropic case where the $Γ$ term is absent. We also confirm that the transitions between the Néel and dimer phases and between the Néel and ferromagnetic phases are continuous transitions governed by Gaussian criticality with central charge $c=1$. The TLL parameter characterizing the critical states at the Gaussian transitions is estimated numerically.

items.title: Damped polarizability and first hyperpolarizability of large systems with hybrid functionals: self-consistent and Lanczos solvers
items.summary: We present a damped coupled-perturbed Kohn-Sham method to compute the dynamical polarizability and first hyperpolarizability of finite systems, implemented in the CRYSTAL code for semi-local, global and range-separated hybrid functionals. The approach is based on the adiabatic time-dependent density functional theory for the complex-valued (hyper)polarizabilities, describing optical phenomena such as absorption, and the nonlinear second-harmonic generation, rectification and Pockels effect. These are obtained either at individual frequencies with a self-consistent solver based on Pulay extrapolation, or at an arbitrary grid of frequency and damping factors with a Lanczos solver, from which the first-order amplitudes required in the hyperpolarizability can be reconstructed. With hybrid functionals, the self-consistent solver tends to become impractical at some point beyond the absorption onset, where there are many excitations for which the external frequency lies between their energy and those of their contributing single-particle transitions, and its convergence eventually stalls for large systems. In contrast, the convergence of the Lanczos method is essentially independent of size, hence the cost of the dynamical response calculation scales with system size as the hybrid ground-state calculation. The implementation is validated in a small molecule and, as an application, we study the first and second-order optical response of a series of hexagonal boron nitride flakes of up to 324 atoms. The use of range-separated hybrid functionals allows to capture the strongly-bound first excitation of the monolayer, and evidences the failure of the self-consistent method to converge excitations with strong electron-hole attraction.

items.title: Higher tensor network states in two spatial dimensions: fundamental theorem for open boundary conditions
items.summary: We introduce a class of two-dimensional tensor network states obtained by categorifying matrix product states. This procedure leads us to consider bond spaces provided by a 2-vector space associated with the 2-cells of the underlying lattice. Tensor network representations are then defined as module categories over the free monoidal category on a monoidal signature encoding the lattice geometry. We prove a fundamental theorem stating that two representations generating the same states with suitable open boundary conditions are equivalent as module categories. Finally, we introduce a notion of 2-injectivity, a categorified analogue of the injectivity condition for matrix product states.

items.title: A Hierarchy of Fast and Strong Signatures for Vertex Orbits
items.summary: The defining features of a physical system are its symmetries and its invariants. For a network, the symmetries are the automorphisms, and the invariants are the vertex orbits they define. Two vertices of a graph may appear structurally indistinguishable without being interchangeable under any graph automorphism. Distinguishing apparent similarity from genuine symmetry lies at the heart of the vertex-orbit partition problem. In this work, we develop a hierarchy of increasingly expressive, automorphism-invariant signatures that draw on the spectral properties of the graph Laplacian and the Dirac operator to reveal subtle structural differences. Guided by a sequence of counterexamples, we progressively strengthen these signatures, ultimately incorporating probing techniques, which are temporary structural perturbations, that expose the hidden distinctions in the original unperturbed graph. We evaluate our approach across diverse benchmark families, recovering exact orbit partitions in challenging instances, including graphs that resist low-dimensional Weisfeiler--Leman refinement. We also examine the computational and numerical limitations of our constructions, distinguishing empirical success from theoretical completeness. Our findings highlight the potential of spectral and probing-based methods for uncovering the structural distinctions that define vertex orbit.

items.title: Compensation Domain Walls in Ferrimagnets as Spin-Torque Oscillator Candidates
items.summary: Spin-torque nano-oscillators are promising nanoscale microwave sources, yet their performance is often limited by narrow operational ranges and sensitivity to device parameters. Here, we numerically investigate the dynamics of compensation domain walls in ferrimagnetic systems driven by spin-transfer torque as a microwave source candidate. These walls arise in structures with adjacent regions of different compensation character, where the competition between exchange and Zeeman energies under an applied magnetic field stabilizes a distinct magnetic texture. We demonstrate steady current-driven rotation of compensation domain walls over a broad range of current densities within the model. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, we develop a collective-coordinate model and derive an analytical expression for the oscillation frequency, which quantitatively reproduces the dependence on current and magnetic field observed in micromagnetic simulations. Our results identify compensation domain walls as a candidate platform for tunable spin-torque nano-oscillators with intrinsic field-induced confinement.

items.title: Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
items.summary: Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in around 3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

items.title: Singlet sector of the vector model with angular potential
items.summary: We study the singlet sector of large-$N$, $O(N)$ vector model on $S^1_β\times S^2_r$ in presence of an angular potential $Ω$. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-ω^2)$, where $ω=rΩ$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-ω^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $ω^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.

items.title: Quantum algorithm for evaluating Lyapunov stability of non-Hermitian systems
items.summary: Stability is a fundamental property of dynamical systems, and Lyapunov theory provides a rigorous link between stability and eigenvalue distribution. By computing eigenvalues, quantum algorithms may offer potential advantages for evaluating the stability of high-dimensional systems under appropriate assumptions regarding data access and quantum resource requirements. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) to efficiently resolve the complex eigenspectrum of non-Hermitian matrices and determine asymptotic stability. By employing block encoding and QSVT techniques, we implement a polynomial transformation to approximate the singular value threshold problem, enabling the localization of eigenvalues with positive real parts under appropriate requirements regarding block encoding efficiency, matrix conditioning, state overlap, and precision. We validate the method numerically on a one-dimensional non-Hermitian spin-1/2 chain with local gain and loss, demonstrating accurate detection of unstable and stable cases, which is consistent with the results obtained by exact diagonalization. These results show that our quantum algorithm is a reliable and powerful tool for stability analysis and spectral characterization of high-dimensional dynamical systems.

items.title: Universal Scaling and Implications of the Apparent Anomalous Hall Voltage of Magnetic Layer with an Adjacent Conducting Layer
authors: Zhihao Yan, Qianbiao Liu, Zhengxiao Li and Lijun Zhu
items.summary: The anomalous Hall voltage of magnetic heterostructures plays a key role via the interplay with a variety of spintronic effects. Under a given electric field (E), the anomalous Hall voltage of a magnetic layer should remain unaffected by adjacent layers unless the latter could modify or contribute to the anomalous Hall conductivity. In this Letter, we report the observation, universality, mechanism, and impacts of the dramatic scaling of the apparent anomalous Hall voltage per electric field (VAH/E) of magnetic heterostructures with the thickness and resistivity of the nonmagnetic conducting layers by combining transport experiments, analytical derivation, and finite-element analyses. We identify that the scaling arises simply from the misreading of the invariant internal anomalous Hall voltage due to the series-resistor effect of the magnetic and nonmagnetic layers within the magnetic heterostructures. The scaling remains strong regardless of the strengths of the spin–orbit torques and spin and orbital Hall conductivities of the normal metals, suggesting that interfacial angular momentum transport plays a minimal role in the anomalous Hall effect. We also show that the harmonic Hall voltage analyses of magnetic heterostructures remain robust against the considerable underestimation of the anomalous Hall voltage and other transverse voltages due to the series-resistor effect. These findings provide crucial information for understanding a variety of spintronic experiments involving the anomalous Hall and other transverse voltages.

We present an alternative derivation of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals based on the quasiclassical matrix kinetic equation. Along with the anomalous Hall effect, anomalous heat flow and anomalous thermoelectric currents are derived.

items.summary: The magnetic ground state of the altermagnet candidate RuO2 remains controversial, with magnetic signatures observed mainly in epitaxial films. Here we show, using first-principles calculations, that magnetism in epitaxial RuO2 can emerge as an interfacial boundary phase at TiO2/RuO2 interfaces. While TiO2-induced epitaxial strain alone does not make (001)-oriented RuO2 magnetic, explicit TiO2/RuO2 interfaces stabilize sizable Ru moments confined to the first few Ru layers. Charge-density and orbital-resolved analyses reveal interfacial electronic reconstruction, and substrate doping provides a route to tune the induced moments. In symmetric TiO2/RuO2/TiO2 heterostructures, the two magnetic interfaces couple through the metallic RuO2 spacer, producing a thickness-dependent alternation between weak-ferromagnetic and compensated altermagnetic states for even RuO2 thicknesses. Our results identify interface engineering as a practical route to stabilize and control fragile magnetism in RuO2.

items.title: Frequency–Angle Acoustic Beam Steering via Nearly Dispersionless Gradient Metasurfaces

items.summary: Gradient metasurfaces provide a powerful platform for wavefront and dynamic beam steering of electromagnetic and acoustic waves by introducing the phase-gradient degree of freedom, but they still suffer from narrow steering angles and low efficiency due to inherent dispersion. Here, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a dispersionless gradient metasurface approach that offers a practical yet powerful route to wide-angle, near-perfect beam steering, overcoming the longstanding trade-off between bandwidth and efficiency in metasurface design. As a proof of concept, we design and fabricate an acoustic metasurface operating at 3430 Hz, which exhibits near-perfect anomalous refraction with an efficiency exceeding 85% over an unprecedented bandwidth of 44.4% (2800–4400 Hz). This performance enables continuous frequency-driven beam steering from 46.5° to 15.8°, covering a 30.7° field of view. Serving as a critical transition between anomalous and normal dispersion, the concept of dispersionless gradient metasurfaces provides a criterion for evaluating the bandwidth limitations of various dispersive counterparts, and establishes a new paradigm for high-performance, frequency-driven dynamic wavefront manipulation.

items.title: The chiral random walk: a quantum-inspired framework for odd diffusion
items.summary: Chirality in active and passive fluids gives rise to odd transport properties, most notably the emergence of robust edge currents that defy standard dissipative dynamics. While these phenomena are well-described by continuum hydrodynamics, the topological analogy with quantum systems, widely invoked to explain their robustness, has lacked a concrete discrete realization. Here, we present a lattice model for an isotropic chiral random walk that bridges the gap between classical stochastic diffusion and unitary quantum evolution. By equipping the walker with an internal degree of freedom and a tunable chirality parameter, , we interpolate between a standard diffusive random walk and a deterministic, topologically non-trivial quantum walk. We show that signatures of the topologically protected edge states characteristic of the unitary limit ( ) persist into the dissipative regime ( ) This correspondence allows us to theoretically ground the robustness of edge flows in classical chiral systems using the bulk-boundary correspondence of Floquet topological insulators. Our results provide a discrete, effective description for odd diffusion, offering a powerful toolkit to predict transport in confined geometries and disordered chiral media.

items.title: The resource theory of causal influence and knowledge of causal influence
authors: Marina Maciel Ansanelli, Beata Zjawin, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, John H Selby, Ciarán M Gilligan-Lee, Ana Belén Sainz and Robert W Spekkens
items.summary: Understanding and quantifying causal relationships between variables is essential for reasoning about the physical world. A challenge to this is the fact that different functional causal models can induce the same conditional probability distribution over observed variables while encoding different amounts of causal influence. Motivated by this observation, we study the underlying functional mechanisms, including uncertainty over them, as meaningful objects in their own right and develop a resource-theoretic framework for quantifying causal influence and knowledge of causal influence. We focus on the simplest nontrivial setting—two variables that are causally ordered, meaning that the first has the potential to influence the second, without hidden confounding. First, we introduce the resource theory that directly quantifies causal influence of a functional dependence in this setting and show that the problem of deciding convertibility of resources and identifying a complete set of monotones has a relatively straightforward solution. Following this, we introduce the resource theory that arises naturally when one has uncertainty about the functional dependence. We describe a linear program for deciding the question of whether one resource (i.e. state of knowledge about the functional dependence) can be converted to another. Then, we focus on the case where the variables are binary. In this case, we identify a triple of monotones that are complete in the sense that they capture the partial order over the set of all resources, and we provide an interpretation of each.

items.title: Quantum criticality beyond thermodynamic stability
authors: Mariam Ughrelidze, Vincent P Flynn, Emilio Cobanera and Lorenza Viola
items.summary: For a many-body system in equilibrium, described by a thermodynamically stable Hamiltonian, quantum criticality is associated with structural changes of the many-body ground state. However, there exist physically relevant models, notably, certain quadratic bosonic Hamiltonians (QBHs), which fail to have a ground state. From a dynamical system-theory standpoint, QBHs can be either dynamically stable or unstable. We show that criticality is a meaningful concept for the entire class of QBHs that are dynamically stable or at the boundary of instability—regardless of thermodynamic stability—and that the key state for such QBHs is a naturally and unambiguously defined quasiparticle vacuum(QPV). This state is Gaussian, and coincides with the ground state if the QBH is thermodynamically stable. We identify a relevant spectral gap, the Krein gap, associated to the minimal spectral separation between creation and annihilation operators, and show that the QPV is unique when the Krein gap is positive. In addition, we prove that, for dynamically stable QBHs with finite-range couplings, correlations are exponentially bounded unless the Krein gap closes—which is associated with one of two kinds of spectral degeneracies: an exceptional point (physically, a free-particle-like collective mode) or a Krein collision (often a bosonic zero mode). As a consequence, long-range correlations can ensue in the QPV. We conclude that (i) the Krein gap takes the role of the spectral gap for dynamically stable QBHs, and (ii) the boundary of dynamical stability and criticality (associated to exceptional points) or multicriticality (associated to Krein collisions) are one and the same. Alongside long-range correlations, we find that bosonic critical behavior beyond thermodynamic stability is witnessed by the scaling of the entanglement entropy and other indicators of equilibrium criticality from information geometry. Hence, our framework opens the door to investigating all dynamically stable QBHs through the lens of critical phenomena, including thermodynamically unstable models from photonics, opto-mechanics, cavity-QED, and magnonics.

items.title: Spaceborne radiation-tolerant atomic-layer memory with on-orbit real-time testing
items.summary: Abstract The human endeavor in space exploration has never ceased, where space electronics with high radiation tolerance are of paramount importance. Due to the atomic-level thin-layer characteristic, atomic-layer material electronic devices exhibit extremely high radiation tolerance compared with traditional bulk material devices. However, on-orbit testing on atomic-layer electronics is still lacking, restricting the understanding of their online performance in the space environment. Here we report a spaceborne radiation-tolerant and low-noise atomic-layer MoS 2 memory array. Deployed on the Fudan No.1 Satellite in a low Earth orbit, this work enables the first demonstration of on-orbit real-time testing on atomic-layer memory. To date, after 23 months of on-orbit testing, the accuracy of the returned memory data has remained at 100%, indicating impressive radiation tolerance. This work presents a substantial step forward for the practical application of atomic-layer space electronics.

items.title: Oxygen-Stoichiometry-Driven Crossover from Polaronic Insulator to Superconductor in Orthorhombic Ti9O10 Films
authors: Zongyao Huang, 宗耀 黄, Wei Hu, 卫 胡, Zhiwei Wang, 智炜 王, Shihao Liu, 仕豪 刘, Huiyu Wang, 慧宇 王, Yanjun Li, 彦君 李, Xiangyu Hua, 翔宇 华, Zhaohang Li, 朝航 李, Feixiong Quan, 飞熊 全, Zhengjie Wang, 郑杰 王, Ying Feng, 颖 冯, Zhen Wang, 臻 王, Jing Tao, 婧 陶, Xigang Luo, 习刚 罗, Jianjun Ying, 剑俊 应, Tao Wu, 涛 吴, Xianhui Chen and 仙辉 陈
items.summary: The Bardeen–Cooper–Schrieffer theory of superconductivity is restricted to weak electron–phonon coupling. In the strong-coupling regime, charge carriers self-trap via local lattice distortions, forming polarons whose condensation provides an alternative mechanism for superconductivity. Titanium oxides serve as a model system for polaron physics, suggesting the possibility of polaronic superconductivity. Here we report oxygen-stoichiometry-driven crossover from polaronic insulator to superconductor in epitaxial Ti9O10 thin films. Temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy supports the films as a potential polaronic insulator, in which oxygen stoichiometry control reveals an anticorrelation between the polaronic insulating state and superconductivity. Tuning the oxygen pressure suppresses the polaronic insulating state and induces superconductivity, resulting in two distinct superconducting regions in the oxygen–pressure phase diagram. Our results provide a pathway toward understanding superconductivity in polaronic materials and offer a route for searching high-temperature superconductors.

items.title: Medium Electrical Conductivity Governs the Collective Behaviors of Quincke Rollers
authors: Zihan Qiao, 子涵 乔, Jingrui Gu, 京瑞 顾, Jiayu Liu, 佳钰 刘, Guomeng Wang, 国猛 王, Hao Lu, 灏 卢, Ting Kuang, 婷 况, Bo Zhang, 波 张, Wei Wang and 威 王
items.summary: Active matter systems can convert environmental energy into continuous motion and exhibit collective behaviors. As a typical electrically driven active particle system, Quincke rollers can display a variety of collective behaviors under a uniform DC electric field. However, a systematic understanding of the emergence and evolution of different collective behaviors is still lacking, and it remains unclear how external environmental conditions, such as temperature and humidity, influence the dynamics of collective behaviors. In this work, we find that increasing temperature and humidity drives a continuous transition of the collective behavior of Quincke rollers from vortices to polar clusters, rotating clusters, and finally active crystals. In situ electrical measurements show that the medium conductivity increases by nearly 10-fold as the temperature rises from 20 ℃ to 60 ℃, and by approximately 30-fold as the relative humidity increases from 5% to 65%, whereas the permittivity changes by about 10−15%. Finite-element calculations further reveal that the increase in medium electrical conductivity strongly modifies the magnitudes of the electric dipolar and hydrodynamic interactions between rollers. These forces shift from pure repulsion to anisotropic attraction and then to isotropic attraction, resulting in the emergence of vortices, polar clusters, rotating clusters, and active crystals in turn. These results provide a simple physical picture linking the conductivity of the medium to the collective states in Quincke roller system and establish a theoretical framework that incorporates dipolar interaction, hydrodynamic interaction, and electro-hydrodynamic interaction for understanding the dynamics of collective behavior. In addition, this work demonstrates that temperature and humidity can serve as simple, efficient, and reversible control parameters for the in situ regulation of the collective behaviors of Quincke rollers.

items.title: Power-Law Quasiperiodic Criticality in a Non-Hermitian Ising Chain
authors: Wen-Long You and 文龙 尤
items.summary: We study a non-Hermitian Ising chain with a power-law quasiperiodic field hj = hcosp(2παj+ϕ), where the positive integer p controls the power of the modulation. The model admits an exact site-factorized similarity transformation that maps the quasi-Hermitian regime onto a real quasiperiodic Ising chain. We derive the exact zero-mode edge-localization boundary and show that the critical field on the quasi-Hermitian branch scales as 2p, while the associated localization-length exponent remains unity for all p. At the boundary, the variance of the logarithmic coupling fluctuations is enhanced exactly by a factor of p2. In the quasi-Hermitian regime, the factorized similarity transformation shows that the spatial biorthogonal entanglement spectrum is identical to that of the Hermitian counterpart. The half-chain entanglement entropy exhibits approximately logarithmic growth over the accessible sizes, with a p-dependent finite-size slope. We finally discuss a possible realization using state-selective loss and conditional no-jump dynamics.

items.summary: Despite their apparent symmetry, halide perovskites can host hidden distortions that affect their properties. Using temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, Glier et al. observed that symmetry-forbidden phonons emerged in the vacancy-ordered double perovskite Cs2SnI6 at low temperatures, despite the persistence of the average cubic structure. A common activation energy of 15–20 meV characterizes the temperature-dependent Raman response, while enhanced multi-phonon scattering highlights strong electron-phonon coupling, demonstrating Raman spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of hidden local structural behavior.

Issue Publication Information
Heesch Weyl fermions in chiral antiferromagnets
authors: Zi-Ting Sun, Xing-Yao Guo, Ruo-Peng Yu, Xue-Jian Gao, Kam Tuen Law
items.summary: Weyl nodes are points in momentum space where two electronic bands touch linearly, each node carrying a chirality that makes it robust against small perturbations. Sun et al. identify Heesch Weyl fermions, symmetry-enforced Weyl nodes pinned at high-symmetry momenta in chiral antiferromagnets without Kramers degeneracy. Symmetry analysis and first-principles calculations reveal candidate materials, higher-order nonlinear Hall responses, and controlled node motion under strain, establishing a magnetic route to high-symmetry Weyl physics.

items.title: Electric-current manipulation of quantum-geometric nonlinear Hall state in a chiral antiferromagnet
authors: Tomohiro Uchimura, Jiahao Han, Yasufumi Araki, Yuta Yamane, Shun Kanai, Jun’ichi Ieda, Hideo Ohno, Shunsuke Fukami
items.summary: Quantum-geometric nonlinear Hall (QgNLH) states characterize the quantum systems that exhibit the nonlinear transverse voltage-current responses with quantum-geometric origins. To functionalize QgNLH states, electrical manipulation is essential but remains challenging. Uchimura et al. demonstrated the electric-current manipulation of the QgNLH state by exploiting the interplay between the QgNLH state and the current-induced spin dynamics in a chiral antiferromagnet. This work opens opportunities for harnessing quantum-geometric nonlinear phenomena in practical devices that are essentially operated by electric current.

items.summary: As a critical fuel of nuclear energy, uranium peroxide precipitation and conversion represent critical steps in uranium extraction processes, directly determining the purity and recovery efficiency of the final product. However, the dynamic mechanism of uranium peroxide precipitation and conversion remains unclear. Here, we investigated the crystallization kinetics of metal peroxides, establishing empirical equations between crystallization rate and solution supersaturation under different metal concentration ranges. Combining the experimental observations with theoretical calculations, we showed that at the lower metal concentration the crystal growth dominates the crystallization process, while at the higher concentration range nucleation becomes the dominant process. Further, mathematical models were developed to correlate crystallization rate with solution composition and operating parameters. Our findings provide fundamental insights to support the development of more efficient and scalable precipitation processes, addressing key challenges in uranium purification and recovery.

authors: Xiaoyang He, 小杨 贺, Chen Chen, 晨 陈, Chuye Quan, 楚烨 全, Shilei Ji, 石磊 季, Jianping Yang, 建平 杨, Xing’ao Li and 兴鳌 李
items.summary: Valleytronics, as an emerging electronic degree of freedom, holds significant potential in low-power devices. However, achieving valley polarization and efficient electron–hole separation remains a challenge. Through first-principles calculations, this study proposes the two-dimensional MXene material Cr2COCl as an ideal platform for valleytronics. The results indicate that Cr2COCl is a ferromagnetic semiconductor with significant valley polarization properties. Its unique layer-resolved orbital contributions enable intrinsic electron–hole separation, thereby effectively suppressing carrier recombination. Biaxial strain linearly modulates valley splitting and Berry curvature, enabling reversible control of the anomalous valley Hall effect. When tensile strain is applied, the system undergoes a topological phase transition, producing a nonzero Chern number (C = 1) and chiral edge states. These findings confirm that Cr2COCl can be used to regulate carriers, adjust valley polarization, and generate topological states through strain engineering, providing a theoretical basis for designing high-performance, low-power valleytronic devices.

items.title: CMOS-compatible ferroelectric artificial dendrite for spatiotemporal integration
authors: Sen Liu, 森 刘, Zi-Hao Hou, 子浩 侯, Peng Yang, 彭 杨, Lei Liu, 磊 刘, Xu Guo, 旭 郭, Nan Li, 楠 李, Zhi-Wei Li, 智炜 李, Yi Sun, 毅 孙, Qing-Jiang Li and 清江 李
items.summary: In biological neural systems, dendrites play an essential role in spatiotemporal information processing, which enables the brain to manage complex tasks with minimal energy. In this study, for the first time, we propose a CMOS-compatible dual-gate ferroelectric thin film transistor (FeTFT) for emulating spatiotemporal information processing in biological dendrites. Owing to the utilization of CMOS-compatible materials and fabrication processes, the FeTFT exhibits exceptional retention characteristics (>106 s) and endurance characteristics (>1012). The following experimental results show that the dendritic spatial and temporal integration can be replicated in the FeTFT device with varying pulse sequences. These superior characteristics, combined with its unique spatiotemporal processing capability, position this novel device as a highly promising candidate for advanced large-scale neuromorphic computing systems, particularly in applications requiring complex signal integration and parallel processing.

items.title: Emergent interweaved CDW unoccupied states in hole-doping LaTe2 with element substitution
authors: Shuya Xing, 淑雅 邢, Hongyu Liu, 宏宇 刘, Xu Chen, 旭 陈, Zhenkai Xie, 圳楷 谢, Zhongxu Wei, 忠旭 魏, Shifeng Zhao, 世峰 赵, Wenping Zhou, 文平 周, Xinqi Li, 新奇 李, Zhihai Cheng and 志海 程
items.summary: Multiple charge density wave (CDW)-ordered layered rare-earth tellurides have increasingly emerged as a research hotspot owing to their unconventional CDW formation, high transition temperatures, and confirmed existence of axial Higgs modes. Recently, interweaved CDWs in LaTe2 and its element-substituted phase LaTe2−xSbx have been investigated through TEM and ARPES measurements, revealing their distinct origins. Nevertheless, several complex diffraction features observed in TEM patterns remain unexplained. In this work, we carried out scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) on LaTe1.6Sb0.4 crystals at 9 K. Three interweaved CDW wave vectors, q1 = 8/11a*, q2 = 5/11a* and q3 = 3/11a*, were observed, which are induced by hole doping in unoccupied states. The q1 and q3 vectors are theoretically verified to be nesting vectors connecting px and py bands. Furthermore, satellite spots relative to the main Bragg spots, corresponding to an 11-a superlattice, have also been detected. Our findings provide critical insights into further exploring the origin of interweaved CDWs in hole- and electron-doped materials.

The parameters were obtained by mapping the model predictions to literature data for the plateau modulus and zero-shear viscosity. Owing to the conversion rules established earlier, the parameters are also expressed in the units used in the multi-chain slip-spring and Kremer–Grest bead–spring models. The latter results are compared with those of earlier studies.

items.title: Mixed spectral statistics in ferrite-loaded microwave billiards
authors: Xiaodong Zhang and 晓东 张
items.summary: We investigate mixed spectral statistics in magnetized ferrite-loaded microwave billiards by resolving the spectrum with respect to the longitudinal quantum number kz. Different longitudinal mode families exhibit distinct random-matrix statistics, leading to the coexistence of Poisson-, GOE-, and GUE-like subspectra in different geometries and frequency regimes. Within the same frequency window, these mode families coexist, giving rise to a complete spectrum that cannot be described by a single random-matrix ensemble. Based on the actual modal composition, we construct mixed random-matrix models as superpositions of statistically independent subspectra. The models reproduce both short-range and long-range spectral correlations without additional fitting parameters. These results show that the mixed spectral statistics is governed by the weighted coexistence of symmetry-distinguished mode families, rather than by a continuous crossover within a single ensemble.

items.title: Application of eigen microstate theory to polymer diffusion
authors: Jiaxin Yu, 佳馨 于, Shengda Zhao, 胜达 赵, Xinghua Zhang and 兴华 张
items.summary: In complex media, polymer diffusion is additionally constrained by geometry and polymer–environment interactions, making the dynamics substantially more complex than those of a freely diffusing Rouse chain and preventing a straightforward mode decomposition. This difficulty motivates us to use eigen microstate theory, which directly extracts dominant modes and their evolution from high-dimensional time-series data, providing a data-driven framework for the dynamical analysis of complex systems. We argue that this framework can be extended to polymer dynamics in porous media or complex polymer architectures. In this work, we take the diffusion of a polymer chain in an idealized two-dimensional model porous medium as a representative example and apply eigen microstate decomposition to the modal analysis of polymer-chain trajectories obtained from molecular dynamics simulations. The decomposition separates the confined chain dynamics into center-of-mass motion and internal conformational motion, and shows that the increasing contribution of the internal component correlates with a renormalization of the chain-length scaling of the long-time diffusion coefficient.

Using this model, we discuss the relationship between the physical properties of IOLs and the formation of glistening, as well as its dynamics.

items.title: Negative viscosity induced by electrohydrodynamic turbulence in nematic liquid crystals
items.summary: Negative viscosity, in which flow is amplified rather than dissipated, represents a striking manifestation of nonequilibrium dynamics. In this review, we summarize recent progress in the study of negative viscosity in electrically driven nematic liquid crystals. Experiments have demonstrated that, under sufficiently strong electric fields, these systems undergo a transition to a turbulent state in which the apparent viscosity becomes negative with a remarkably large magnitude. This regime is characterized by spontaneous shear flow under zero applied stress, nonmonotonic flow curves, and self-oscillation. Systematic studies of different materials reveal that the magnitude of negative viscosity depends sensitively on electrical properties such as dielectric permittivity and conductivity. Numerical simulations based on a Q-tensor framework successfully reproduce spontaneous shear flow and nonlinear flow curves, providing insight into the underlying mechanism. In particular, the coupling among director distortions, space-charge generation, and flow, mediated by disclinations, is identified as the key mechanism. These results establish electrically driven nematic liquid crystals as a platform for exploring nonequilibrium rheology.

items.summary: Fluxonium qubits are promising candidates for fault-tolerant quantum processors, but their dispersive readout remains challenging due to measurement-induced state transitions (MIST) that populate higher-excited states. To address this, the authors systematically explore MIST across a broad range of fluxonium parameters using branch analysis. They find that lighter fluxoniums are less susceptible to these transitions than heavier counterparts, and trace this to three key mechanisms. These results provide a path toward optimizing fluxonium design for fast, high-fidelity readout.

The common vortex size also allows distinct OAM states to overlap and interfere on the same ring, producing programmable petal-like pressure patterns. These capabilities could facilitate acoustic multiplexing and detection, and structured-wave sensing and particle manipulation.

This study shows that applying four non-coplanar bias fields breaks this deadlock, revealing both quantities at once. This self-calibration could enable nanodiamond sensing in complex environments such as living cells and aqueous solutions, where precalibrating the sensor is not an option.
